title: Control choice and reproducibility of dataset-specific emodin expression signatures in breast cancer
content:
by Liang Cai, Quanlei Wang, Jingxian Cao, Junrui Hu

A public drug-expression profile is defined by its experimental comparison. We examined the dependence of breast cancer emodin signatures on comparator choice and preprocessing, using 212 GSE85871 arrays and a fixed 77-gene signature from two emodin arrays compared with other active compounds. Reprocessing retained expression direction more often than threshold-defined membership. In a post hoc common-model analysis without the operational effect-size filter, pooled unmatched-vehicle lists were much larger, yet contained 66.7% and 73.3% of the active-compound genes before and after reprocessing. Low Jaccard overlap therefore combined list expansion with partial membership changes. Independent 48-hour exposures gave partial directional agreement but weak genome-wide recurrence. At 6 hours, the measurable signature subset passed expression-matched random-set tests and separately corrected post hoc rotation tests at the four higher concentrations. In a 26-donor single-cell atlas, the score did not exceed matched localization references. The main adjusted survival hazard ratio in 3,114 patients was 1.128 per standard deviation (nominal 95% confidence interval 1.007–1.264), but failed two-signature correction (q = 0.0758). Unresolved discovery vehicle matching and small exposure experiments, with two samples per condition at 48 hours and three independent cultures at 6 hours, limit interpretation. These results call for comparator-specific interpretation of public signatures; observational patient associations cannot establish emodin efficacy or predict treatment response.
